<description>
This PR fixes the `interface_ipc*.py` tests, which have been [failing](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037#issuecomment-6082043240) on NetBSD since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037.

As file descriptor budget regressions of this kind recur (see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31537 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36078), the macOS CI job now models NetBSD's limit so they are caught before merging rather than by nightly NetBSD CI afterwards.

See the commit messages for details.
</description>

<commits>
956f807bdb qa, refactor: Move `-maxconnections` budget into named constant

Easy to review using the following:
```
git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change
```

62571e7e67 qa: Account for `-ipcbind` file descriptors in `-maxconnections`

Since `-ipcbind` reserves one listening socket plus
`ipc::DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (16) client slots in `min_required_fds`,
the framework's `-maxconnections=76` no longer fits the 256 file
descriptor budget on NetBSD, and every `interface_ipc*.py` node starts
with "Warning: Reducing -maxconnections ...", which the framework treats
as a failure.

Lower `-maxconnections` by that reservation on IPC-enabled nodes only,
so the rest of the suite keeps its P2P connection slots.

311bc7c3bb ci: Enforce NetBSD's 256 file descriptor budget in the macOS job

On select()-based platforms such as NetBSD, `bitcoind` can use at most
`FD_SETSIZE` (256) file descriptors, so the functional test framework
pins `-maxconnections` to that budget. Any change that grows
`min_required_fds` then makes every node print "Warning: Reducing
-maxconnections ...", which the framework treats as a failure. Such
regressions are currently caught only by nightly NetBSD CI (see #31537,

Add a `CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT` knob that runs functional test node processes
through a wrapper capping `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, and enable it for the macOS
native job with NetBSD's value of 256.
</commits>

--- /dev/null
+++ b/ci/test/wrap-fd-limit.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# Copyright (c) The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit/.
+#
+# Run a command with RLIMIT_NOFILE capped at $CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT.
+#
+# On select()-based platforms such as NetBSD, bitcoind can use at most
+# FD_SETSIZE (256) file descriptors regardless of the RLIMIT_NOFILE. Capping the
+# hard limit here makes RaiseFileDescriptorLimit() return the same number on any
+# platform, so an fd-budget regression (e.g. a new "Reducing -maxconnections ..."
+# warning on stderr, which the functional test framework treats as a failure) is
+# caught by this job instead of only on NetBSD.
+
+export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
+set -o errexit
+
+ulimit -S -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}"
+ulimit -H -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}"
+exec "$@"
diff --git a/test/functional/test_framework/util.py b/test/functional/test_framework/util.py
index 7dbf978e4e..6f982f82d9 100644
--- a/test/functional/test_framework/util.py
+++ b/test/functional/test_framework/util.py
@@ -522,6 +522,29 @@ def initialize_datadir(dirname, n, chain, disable_autoconnect=True):
     return datadir
 
 
+# Limit max connections to mitigate test failures on some systems caused by the warning:
+# "Warning: Reducing -maxconnections from <...> to <...> due to system limitations".
+# For details, consult the `AppInitParameterInteraction` function in src/init.cpp.
+#  available_fds = 256                // Same as FD_SETSIZE on NetBSD.
+#                                     // Enforced in CI via CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT (macOS native job).
+#  MIN_CORE_FDS = 151                 // Number of file descriptors required for core functionality.
+#  MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS = 8        // Maximum number of -addnode outgoing nodes.
+#  num_p2p_bind = 3                   // Maximum number of bound P2P interfaces (-bind and -whitebind) used in a test.
+#  num_rpc_bind = 2                   // Maximum number of HTTP sockets used in a test.
+#  DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS = 16  // Reserved for connected HTTP clients.
+#
+#  min_required_fds = MIN_CORE_FDS + MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS + num_p2p_bind + num_rpc_bind + DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS =
+#    = 151 + 8 + 3 + 2 + 16 = 180;
+#  num_p2p_max_connections = available_fds - min_required_fds = 256 - 180 = 76;
+TEST_MAX_P2P_CONNECTIONS = 76
+# File descriptors reserved by a single default -ipcbind listener: one listening
+# socket plus ipc::DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS (16) client connection slots.
+# Nodes started with -ipcbind subtract this from TEST_MAX_P2P_CONNECTIONS to
+# stay within the same budget. A test that configures more IPC listeners or slots
+# than that must lower -maxconnections itself.
+IPC_RESERVED_FDS = 1 + 16
+
+
 def write_config(config_path, *, n, chain, extra_config="", disable_autoconnect=True):
     # Translate chain name to config name
     if chain == 'main':
@@ -563,20 +586,7 @@ def write_config(config_path, *, n, chain, extra_config="", disable_autoconnect=
         f.write("unsafesqlitesync=1\n")
         if disable_autoconnect:
             f.write("connect=0\n")

-        #  MIN_CORE_FDS = 151                 // Number of file descriptors required for core functionality.
-        #  MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS = 8        // Maximum number of -addnode outgoing nodes.
-        #  num_p2p_bind = 3                   // Maximum number of bound P2P interfaces (-bind and -whitebind) used in a test.
-        #  num_rpc_bind = 2                   // Maximum number of HTTP sockets used in a test.
-        #  DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS = 16  // Reserved for connected HTTP clients.
-        #
-        #  min_required_fds = MIN_CORE_FDS + MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS + num_p2p_bind + num_rpc_bind + DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS =
-        #    = 151 + 8 + 3 + 2 + 16 = 180;
-        #  num_p2p_max_connections = available_fds - min_required_fds = 256 - 180 = 76;
-        f.write("maxconnections=76\n")
+        f.write(f"maxconnections={TEST_MAX_P2P_CONNECTIONS}\n")
         f.write("par=" + str(min(2, os.cpu_count())) + "\n")
         # Use a single prevoutfetch worker thread to keep per-node resource usage low.
         f.write("prevoutfetchthreads=1\n")
